categories.label: Banana
categories.use: Use when the human explicitly approves a node, edge, decision, or statement.

categories.label: Opera
categories.meaning: AI inference / speculative interpretation / dramatic extrapolation.
categories.use: Use when the agent inferred something plausible that still needs confirmation.

categories.label: Jester
categories.meaning: Critique / contradiction / architectural skepticism / bullshit detection.
categories.use: Use when the map should highlight a challenge, contradiction, or skeptical read.

categories.label: Dumpster Fire
categories.meaning: Known risk / dangerous shortcut / entropy hotspot / technical debt.
categories.use: Use when a concept is already known to be dangerous or likely to fail.

categories.label: Hive
categories.meaning: Reusable learning / organizational knowledge / proven pattern.
categories.use: Use for knowledge that should carry across sessions or projects.

categories.label: Fog
categories.meaning: Unknowns / ambiguity / missing evidence / unclear ownership.
categories.use: Use when the map needs to preserve uncertainty instead of pretending certainty.

categories.label: Spark
categories.meaning: New idea / emerging concept / experimental direction.
categories.use: Use for promising but immature concepts.

categories.label: Law
categories.meaning: Rule / governance / mandatory constraint / architecture standard.
categories.use: Use for non-negotiable constraints and project rules.

categories.label: Thread
categories.meaning: Cross-system dependency / conceptual linkage / shared context.
categories.use: Use for relationships that connect this map to a larger system.

categories.label: Lab Rat
categories.meaning: Experimental feature / unsafe prototype / operational test.
categories.use: Use for POCs and tests that should not be treated as production-ready.

categories.label: Ghost
categories.meaning: Stale concept / abandoned direction / zombie architecture.
categories.use: Use for ideas that still exist in the map but should not guide current work.

categories.label: Siren
categories.meaning: Critical alert / rule failure / security issue / major drift.
categories.use: Use when attention should stop and move to the flagged issue.

modelNote: Categories are separate from core node type. A node can be a concept, decision, risk, question, or evidence while also carrying one or more category labels.
